fixes.explanation: That's right, friend. The writer says, “So do not be surprised, brothers, if the world hates you.” He doesn't tell them the world will love them. He tells them not to be surprised if it hates them. A heads-up like that beats getting caught off guard.

The writer says something different, friend. He says, “And by this we will know that we belong to the truth…” It's the truth, not the world. He says it right after telling his little children to love in action and truth. The world doesn't show up in that line at all.

That's not what the writer says, friend. He says, “Even if our hearts condemn us, God is greater than our hearts…” He doesn't say God agrees with a condemning heart. He says God is greater than our hearts. He adds that God “knows all things.”

That's it, friend. The writer says, “And by this we know that He remains in us: by the Spirit He has given us.” The Spirit is a gift God gave, and that's how we know. I spent years in a junk drawer wondering if anybody remembered me, so I can tell you a gift like that means a lot.

Dreams don't show up in this verse, friend. The writer says, “And by this we know that He remains in us: by the Spirit He has given us.” The answer is the Spirit God has given us. Nobody has to wait for bedtime to find out. Your pillow can take the night off.
